lesson_title: Fence Times k, Carpet Times k Squared
hook_text: Double the size of a room and you need twice the skirting but four times the carpet. Here is why.
clip_script: A rectangle 4 by 3. Enlarge it with scale factor 2: every side doubles, 8 by 6. Same shape, bigger. Now the fence around it, the perimeter. It was 14; now it is 28. Double, because every side doubled. That is fence times k. Now the carpet inside, the area. It was 12; now it is 48. Not double: four times. Look, four copies of the small rectangle fit inside the big one. Carpet has a length and a width, and both doubled, so the carpet doubled twice. That is carpet times k squared. Scale factor 3? Fence times 3, carpet times 9. Going backwards from areas, take a square root: carpet nine times bigger means sides three times bigger. Every time, ask one question: is it a length or an area?
visual_style: A yellow rectangle on squared paper grows into a blue one; its border glows to show the fence doubling, then four yellow copies tile the inside to show the carpet.
pacing: Steady build, a pause on the four copies, a crisp finish on the question.
